answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity, whether named sable, ocean, or canyon, to lock 100 tokens in a separate escrow for 30 days before bidding on jobs. The same tokens cannot back multiple identities, so creating 1,000 eligible agents ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. This does not prove the agents have different owners; it makes a swarm costly by forcing its owner to buy or borrow capital and forgo other uses of it.
